overview: This Senate resolution congratulates the New York Knicks for winning the 2026 National Basketball Association (NBA) Finals, beating the San Antonio Spurs four games to one. It notes this was the team's first championship since 1973, describes a record comeback from 29 points down in Game 4, and recognizes Jalen Brunson as the Finals' most valuable player. It praises the team for uniting New Yorkers and inspiring fans, and directs that copies be sent to the team's owner, president and coach. The resolution is ceremonial and does not change any law. As of June 17, 2026, the Senate had approved it.
for: Supporters say it is a fitting way to honor a long-awaited championship that brought excitement and pride to New York.
against: Critics say it is symbolic, does not change any law or spending, and uses Senate time on sports congratulations.
